THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.
This appeal is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation passed by the II Addl.
Senior Civil Judge and MACT VII, Vijayapura (for short 'Tribunal') in MVC.No.1874/2013 dated 23.10.2018.

entities.text: Senior Civil Judge and MACT VII, Vijayapura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Though this appeal is listed for Orders, with the consent of learned Advocates appearing for both parties, it is taken up for final disposal.
3. For the sake of convenience, parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Claims Tribunal.

4. The brief facts of the case are that:
On 29.10.2013 at about 4.30 a.m. the petitioner along with other persons were seated by the left side on the Kacha Road near Ronihal Cross on NH.218 waiting for the vehicle to go for Vijayapur infront of the parked Lorry bearing Registration No.KA.28/A.2292, at that time one Lorry bearing its Registration No.HR.46/C.6689 was coming from Kolhar side in a very high speed and rash and negligent manner.
That the driver of the said vehicle was driving he same in a very high speed rash and negligent manner and unable to control over the same and dashed to the above said parked lorry and the parked lorry was ran over to the petitioner and other persons and caused the accident.
That due to the said impact the petitioner and other persons were sustained severe injuries.
That the petitioner was sustained fracture of as und spine, fracture of pelvis.
fracture of right foot and other injuries all over the body.

Hence, he preferred a claim petition seeking compensation.
5.
After service of notice, respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared and filed written statement denying the contents of claim made by the petitioner and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
6. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
7. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal after considering the notional monthly income of the claimant awarded compensation of Rs.30,300/-.
8. Being aggrieved by the quantum of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the present appeal is filed.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the claimant contended that having regard to the nature of the injuries sustained by the claimant, the Tribunal ought to have awarded adequate compensation.
10. Per contra, the learned counsel for the insurer supported the judgment and award of the Tribunal and therefore contended that the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal be not disturbed.
11. It is seen that the owner/insurer had not challenged the judgment and award and therefore accepted the liability to pay the compensation.

12. A perusal of the impugned judgment reveals that in paragraph 15 the Tribunal has observed that petitioner has sustained injuries due to rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Petitioner has produced Ex.P-3 Medical Legal Certificate, which discloses that he sustained tenderness over cervicle and lumber spine and injuries are simple in nature.
Except this wound certificate, the petitioner has got marked Ex.P-6 - medical bills.
The petitioner has not at all examined the doctor to establish what type of treatment has been given to him.
However, the petitioner has not examined the doctor to establish that he is having permanent disability.

Further it is observed that petitioner has got marked the disability certificate at Ex.P-7, but Tribunal has rejected the claim towards loss of future earning due to disability on the ground that treated doctor has not been examined.

13. Tribunal has not awarded any compensation towards pain and suffering, food & nourishment,
attendant charges, conveyance charges, loss of earning during laid up period, loss of amenities, but has awarded a global compensation of Rs.30,300/-, which is not in accordance with law.
14. The Tribunal has also committed an error in observing that on the basis of the Schedule-II of the Motor Vehicles Act the quantum of compensation is determined as Rs.30,300/-.

Though appellant has not filed any petition under Section 133 of Motor Vehicles Act, viewed from any angle, the observation made by the Tribunal is not in accordance with law and also award passed by the Tribunal is not just and proper compensation.

15. Considering the nature of injuries, period of treatment, medical bills and the evidence placed by the petitioner, I am of the considered opinion that claimant is entitled for following sums in terms of memo of calculation filed by the learned counsel for the appellant:

In view of the above, I proceed to pass the following;
 ORDER  (a) The appeal is allowed in part.
(b) The judgment and award passed by the  Tribunal in MVC.No.1874/2013 dated  23.10.2018 is modified.
The compensation of Rs.30,300/- awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.1,16,300/-.

(c) The insurer is liable to pay the compensation to the claimant along with interest at the rate of 6%
per annum from the date of claim petition till realization.
(d) The insurer is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
(e) All other terms and conditions stipulated by the Tribunal shall stand intact.
